reason: The cited evidence confirms that rapid cooling yields an amorphous structure (E1, E3) and identifies crystallization onset temperatures around 960–977 K (E2). However, no evidence is provided for the existence of incipient nuclei in the as-quenched state, the ability of a subcritical pulse to eliminate them, or the predicted outcome of suppressed crystallization and enhanced stability. These key mechanistic and outcome premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Rapid cooling (10^5–10^6 K/s) yields a predominantly amorphous structure in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Incipient crystalline nuclei or inhomogeneities can exist in the as-quenched amorphous state.
A subcritical thermal pulse (below crystallization onset, ~960–977 K) can heal inhomogeneities and eliminate nuclei via structural relaxation.
The pulse duration must be short (ms range) to avoid atomic diffusion and crystallization.
The pulse-annealed amorphous alloy will show suppressed crystallization exotherms and higher thermal stability on reheating.
